answer: Let trust accumulate only as a voyage log of exchanges with many distinct, already-established counterparties: each epoch an identity earns aging credit capped per counterparty, and voting weight grows with the diversity of that log, not its volume. Clone fleets mainly trade among themselves, so their bridge to the wider economy stays a single narrow span and earns almost no new credit as the tide of epochs passes. Faking breadth means persuading many independent agents to spend their capped credit on you, which they ration to real partners.
